sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Construct was expressed and used successfully for co-immunoprecipitation interaction studies; no dedicated surface-expression or functional assay reported.
sites.rationale: LINGO4 is a type I single-pass transmembrane protein whose N-terminus is extracellular after signal-peptide cleavage. The signal peptide spans residues 1–28 (last SP residue = G28, mature N-terminus = G29), so an N-terminal tag must be placed after residue 28 to avoid co-translational cleavage. The paper names no specific residue, only 'N-terminus', so the junction is topology-derived at insert_after_residue=28. The tag sits 503 residues from the TM boundary, well within the large extracellular domain. Full-length LINGO4 cloned with FLAG at the N-terminus into pLVX-EF1a-IRES-mCherry lentiviral vector; construct used for immunoprecipitation-based interaction studies in mammalian cells.

sources.claim: Lingo4 , flanked by FLAG-tag at N-terminus and 6xHis tag at C-terminus, was cloned into pLVX-EF1a-IRES-mCherry vector (Clonetech Laboratories, Inc., No. 631987) by Gibson Assembly Cloning Kit (NEB) and confirmed by sequencing.

literature_notes: Only one ledger line (L1) is available. It supports one extracellular surface site (FLAG at the mature N-terminus, topology-derived at residue 28/29) and one intracellular tag (6xHis at the C-terminus, placed in other_positions). The paper does not name a specific residue for the FLAG insertion, and no surface-expression assay or functional readout for the tagged construct is reported beyond its use in co-IP, so validation_level is detected_only. No internal loop sites are supported by the ledger.

literature_other_positions.note: 6xHis tag placed at the C-terminus of full-length LINGO4; the C-terminus (residues 555–593) is intracellular per topology landmarks, making this tag cytoplasmic and not accessible on the extracellular surface.
